about: The world plan's height classes (docs/design/world-squares.md section 2; Chem.WorldPlan reads this and world/squares/). Each world square takes one band; touching world squares differ by at most "step" bands. A band's height is the land it stands at in metres, before its biome's own base and relief. "slots" is how many places a feature may cross a side (one a chunk). "shore" is the shoreline's offset classes in cells from a side that faces the sea: two sides of one shore take the same class where they meet, so a coast runs on. "wall" is the band of an east-west world's north and south edge rows, which nothing crosses. A square template (world/squares/<id>.json) names its bands, its anchor biome (world/biomes.json), its weight in the solver's roll, its landmark intents (world/landmarks/) with "where" rules, and per side (n, e, s, w as it lies unturned; slots run west to east on n and s, north to south on e and w) the features it offers, each a road, river (flowing in or out), range or canyon at a slot, a "must" or a "may", and "coast" if that side may face the sea. "ends" says how a feature may stop inside it (a river in a lake, a range fading, a canyon closing). "rotate" lets the solver turn it a quarter at a time; "repeats" frees it from the rule that copies stand at least 3 world squares apart; "filler" marks a band's template that fits anything; "pinned" is the valley's; "pass" a range crossing.
